findings.title: Provision native tools in the hygiene CI job
findings.defect: The new top-level unittest-discovered mutation and coverage regressions require mutmut and diff-cover, but the hygiene Actions job installs only graphviz, python3-yaml and python3-pytest. The new requirements install is in the separate backend job and cannot provision hygiene.
findings.scenario: A clean hygiene runner discovers these new tests and fails before exercising their behavior. With PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and the already installed Python test runner, the candidate produces 3 failed / 1 passed: missing mutmut, missing diff-cover, and the expected semantic coverage GAP replaced by missing-tool GAP.
findings.suggested_fix: Provision the required native-tool closure, pinned and hash-verified, in the job that executes these tests; preserve the native positive and negative cases rather than skipping them. Keep the quick hygiene gate's added cost explicit.
write_set: a checked-in hash-pinned CI tool requirements file
findings.escape: The repair's clean environment simulation exercised gate backend, while full hygiene was run only on an already provisioned host.
findings.verification: In a fresh isolated environment with only declared CI dependencies, hygiene and the native mutation/coverage regression tests pass; missing-tool negative checks still fail closed.

findings.title: Make linked-token delivery recoverable on poll retry
findings.defect: The first GET poll irrevocably completes the link and returns the only copy of the bearer token. Every later poll returns linked without a token. The completion write also precedes session persistence.
findings.scenario: Confirm a device, let the first GET /v1/link execute but discard its response (ordinary connection loss), then repeat the same GET. It returns HTTP 200 {state: linked} with no token, while a TV that never received the token still gets 401 from GET /v1/profile. The user must start a new link flow despite the server reporting success.
findings.suggested_fix: Make completion and token delivery retryable while preserving one-time customer confirmation and hash-only credential storage. Ensure persistence cannot leave a completed link without a usable session; revise the test and OpenAPI wording that codify one-shot delivery.
findings.escape: Tests retain the first response and explicitly assert that later polls omit the token; no dropped-response/retry scenario is exercised.
findings.verification: Discard a successful linked poll response and retry; the same authorized device can still obtain a usable session, with no raw secret persisted and no confirm replay or foreign-profile access.

findings.title: Enforce the response-size contract before saving a profile
findings.defect: Only request size is checked. The profile envelope adds bytes after a maximum-size accepted request, and _respond serializes without any response bound.
findings.scenario: PUT /v1/profile with revision 0 and fantasySelections='x'*65490 serialized with compact separators is exactly 65,536 bytes. It returns 200 with a 65,632-byte body, persists revision 1, and GET returns the same oversized body. This violates CONTRACT-AFC-P2-API's request and response limit.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the serialized profile envelope's byte length before mutation, and enforce the response cap consistently. Reject an update that cannot be returned within the contract without persisting it. Cover escaping/UTF-8 expansion as well as ASCII.
findings.escape: The added exact-limit test uses POST /v1/link, whose response is small, rather than a profile that echoes user data inside a larger envelope.
findings.verification: Boundary-sized updates either return a <=65,536-byte envelope or return a structured 400 with the prior profile unchanged; subsequent GET responses stay within the limit.

findings.title: Validate profile selector types before set construction
findings.defect: An authenticated request's body.profileId is inserted into a Python set before validation. JSON arrays and objects are unhashable and fall into the generic service-unavailable handler.
findings.scenario: An authenticated PUT /v1/profile with {profileId: [], revision: 1, data: {}} (or profileId: {}) returns 503 unavailable instead of the required 400 malformed input. The service logs TypeError and a client may retry a permanently invalid request.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate explicitly supplied profile selectors against the ProfileId string contract before comparing them, and compare values without requiring caller-controlled values to be hashable.
findings.escape: Foreign-profile tests only pass strings; malformed JSON tests validate the top-level object but not selector types.
findings.verification: Array/object/null/non-string selectors return structured 400 without mutation; a valid foreign string remains 403 and a valid own-profile request still succeeds.

findings.title: Restrict DynamoDB grants to each function's operations
findings.defect: DynamoDBCrudPolicy gives ApiFunction write/delete/batch-write access to Alerts although its alerts route only reads. Every CRUD grant also includes deletion even though the shared store exposes only get, put, update and query and no current or declared delete operation.
findings.scenario: The generated execution role authorizes ApiFunction to forge or delete any profile's alert records, and gives other CRUD roles unnecessary delete capability. If code or a dependency in a function is compromised, IAM does not contain it to its assigned data operations. Offline inspection of SAM 1.169.0's actual policy template proves these Allow actions; this is not a claim of a demonstrated remote code-execution exploit.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace broad CRUD templates with explicit per-function action/resource statements derived from the table-operation inventory. Give the API only read access to Alerts, remove unneeded DeleteItem/BatchWriteItem grants, and preserve the required Links index and stream permissions.
findings.escape: Template tests validate service types, routes and SSM presence, but never inspect expanded DynamoDB actions by function.
findings.verification: Offline expanded-role inspection proves required operations remain allowed and unrelated writes/deletes are absent; SAM lint and backend tests remain green.

findings.title: Deliver the deployed auth/API test allocation owned by B01T
findings.defect: Only the offline Moto fixture and unit/contract suites were delivered. The shared deployed fixture and device_auth/api test directories explicitly assigned to P2-B01T are absent, without an owner scope amendment deferring their authorship.
findings.scenario: The next deployed verification command cannot collect B01's auth/API cases: python3.12 -m pytest --collect-only -q -p no:cacheprovider backend/tests/deployed exits 4 with 'file or directory not found' and no tests. Deferring actual deployed execution to L02/L03 does not deliver the test artifacts those slices must execute.
findings.suggested_fix: Author the allocated deployed conftest and auth/API cases against the declared contracts, keep them separate from the offline gate, and record execution as NOT_RUN until the authorized dev-stack lease and owner actions are available. Do not replace deployed evidence with Moto results.
write_set: backend/tests/conftest.py (only if needed to scope offline fixtures)
findings.escape: The red inventory froze 65 offline assertions but did not reconcile the explicit deployed-path allocation in the approved planning package.
findings.verification: Offline collection finds the named deployed cases without contacting AWS; actual execution remains a separately recorded L02/L03 obligation, with absent prerequisites a typed gap rather than PASS.

leads.title: Device/user-code brute force
leads.proof: backend/template.yaml:64-66 configures DefaultRouteSettings at rate 5 and burst 10, and the frozen template test checks both are nonzero. device_auth.issue selects eight characters independently from 32 symbols (40 bits), expires the pending code after 600 s, and creates a separate 256-bit polling handle. confirm validates the SSM passphrase before it can bind a code. Guessing a displayed code alone cannot retrieve the bearer session. API Gateway limits are best-effort targets, not a strict per-code attempt counter; real deployed enforcement is still unverified.

leads.title: Remote device-code phishing
leads.proof: This manual, single-owner design necessarily grants access to the client whose code the authenticated owner confirms. /link says 'Link your TV', explicitly tells the user to enter the code shown on their TV, leaves the code empty, and requires a deliberate submit plus the SSM passphrase; it does not prefill or auto-confirm a query-supplied code. A victim deliberately entering an attacker's code can still authorize that client, an inherent social-engineering risk of device flows rather than a demonstrated bypass of this contract. The current possession instruction is meaningful mitigation. Stronger warnings/device context could harden it, but are not treated as a missing normative requirement or fixable product defect in B01.

leads.title: DynamoDB least privilege
leads.proof: The table resources are scoped, but actions are broader than each function needs. SAM's installed policy template expands DynamoDBCrudPolicy to Allow DeleteItem and BatchWriteItem, including ApiFunction on Alerts. No API operation writes/deletes generated alerts and no store accessor deletes any item.

leads.title: Pipeline no-mutate pragma
leads.proof: The exclusion is explicit and narrowly justified by the frozen AST contract in test_backend_template.py:107-122, which requires direct calls in the handler body that mutmut replaces with a trampoline. The added behavioral test executes INSERT/MODIFY/REMOVE and empty batches, verifies call order/arguments and verifies routed alerts in Moto DynamoDB. The four future-module substitutes are explicit monkeypatches and do not pretend to be deployed module evidence. Thus this is not hidden untested wiring. Its limitation remains real: the native mutation inventory measures _game_events but contains zero lambda_handler mutants, so the reported score must not be described as native mutation coverage of the pipeline orchestration. Revisit this exemption when the stubs are realized.

leads.title: Inline-script Content-Security-Policy
leads.proof: unsafe-inline is replaceable with a hash/nonce or a separate same-origin script; it is not intrinsically necessary. However the handler returns a constant local HTML file, never interpolates request/secret content, the script writes responses with textContent, code is manually entered, and framing is denied. No reachable HTML/script injection was found. The current policy is a defense-in-depth weakness, not an evidenced XSS defect; a script hash would be a small optional hardening change.

leads.title: Disabled ingest schedule default
leads.proof: The complete minute schedule exists and its State references an ENABLED/DISABLED parameter. B01 deliberately ships an unimplemented ingest stub, while live activation is separately controlled. Starting with DISABLED avoids invoking that stub continuously and is consistent with only running for relevant live games after B02/activation. It is not evidence that game-window activation is implemented or accepted.

leads.title: Mutation retries and loaded-host timeouts
leads.proof: The final adapter changes the documented timeout_constant/timeout_multiplier from defaults to 5/30. Earlier exit-3 runs were not accepted as passes; timeouts remain UNRESOLVED. An independent final-config run on the exact candidate exited 0 in 641.745 seconds, scoring 1376 killed / 1383 with 7 survivors and zero timeouts or unresolved states; observed host load immediately afterward was about 19.5/24.4/20.5 (1/5/15 min), not a controlled stress qualification. This supports a repaired timeout calibration, not a confirmed continuing flaky gate. The first two raw logs are absent from the committed evidence, so their disjoint-timeout explanation remains author-reported, and this is one verification run rather than a statistical reliability claim.
